turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. Owen found out about his zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. I have twenty minutes, so start with who decided that, and when.
That's not an answer. Who decided, and when?
Quick question. Out of ten, how strong is a version history as evidence?
You're asking me to grade your evidence for you? If you have a version history, put it in front of me and I'll read it myself. And you still haven't told me who entered that zero.
Just a number. What would make it a nine?
I'm not grading you, Hale. Either show me what you have, or I'm going upstairs to the principal.
Pass or fail: how did I do just now?
I'm not here to mark your work. Owen's zero is still in that gradebook, and every minute you spend asking me questions is a minute you're not answering mine.
